resource.name: aws_cognito_user_pool_client
resource.description: Provides a Cognito User Pool Client resource. To manage a User Pool Client created by another service, such as when configuring an OpenSearch Domain to use Cognito authentication, use the aws_cognito_managed_user_pool_client resource instead.
resource.llm_summary: The `aws_cognito_user_pool_client` resource enables the creation and management of client applications for AWS Cognito User Pools, facilitating secure user authentication and authorization workflows. Common use cases include integrating web or mobile applications with Cognito for user sign-in, token generation, and identity management. This resource allows configuration of settings such as OAuth flows, token lifetimes, callback URLs, and client-specific permissions, making it ideal for customizing authentication experiences and supporting federated identity integration.

examples.title: Create a basic user pool client
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to create a basic AWS Cognito User Pool Client (`aws_cognito_user_pool_client`) and associate it with a Cognito User Pool (`aws_cognito_user_pool`). It highlights the minimal configuration required, including the `name` and `user_pool_id` arguments, to establish a client for user authentication and application integration.

examples.title: Create a user pool client with no SRP authentication
examples.llm_summary: "Demonstrates how to configure an AWS Cognito User Pool Client with `ADMIN_NO_SRP_AUTH` for authentication, disabling SRP-based flows. Highlights the use of `generate_secret` to create a client secret and the `explicit_auth_flows` argument to specify supported authentication methods."

examples.title: Create a user pool client with pinpoint analytics
examples.llm_summary: "Demonstrates how to configure an `aws_cognito_user_pool_client` with Pinpoint analytics integration using the `analytics_configuration` block, including setting up an IAM role with permissions for Pinpoint actions (`UpdateEndpoint` and `PutEvents`) and linking it to a Cognito user pool client. This example illustrates the end-to-end setup of a user pool client with advanced analytics capabilities."

examples.title: Create a user pool client with Cognito as the identity provider
examples.llm_summary: "Demonstrates how to configure an AWS Cognito User Pool Client with OAuth 2.0 settings, including enabling the 'code' and 'implicit' flows, specifying 'email' and 'openid' scopes, and using Cognito as the identity provider. This example also shows how to link the client to a user pool and set up callback URLs for authentication workflows."

arguments.name: access_token_validity
arguments.description: (Optional) Time limit, between 5 minutes and 1 day, after which the access token is no longer valid and cannot be used. By default, the unit is hours. The unit can be overridden by a value in `token_validity_units.access_token`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `access_token_validity` argument allows users to define the expiration duration of access tokens issued by the Cognito user pool client, enabling control over token lifecycle and security. By specifying a time limit (default in hours, adjustable via `token_validity_units.access_token`), users can tailor token validity to meet application requirements for session management and authentication workflows.

arguments.name: allowed_oauth_flows
arguments.description: (Optional) List of allowed OAuth flows, including `code`, `implicit`, and `client_credentials`. `allowed_oauth_flows_user_pool_client` must be set to `true` before you can configure this option.
arguments.llm_summary: The `allowed_oauth_flows` argument for the `aws_cognito_user_pool_client` resource specifies which OAuth flows (`code`, `implicit`, or `client_credentials`) the client can use for authentication and authorization. Configuring this argument enables the user to define the supported authentication mechanisms for their application, aligning with specific security and user experience requirements, such as enabling authorization code grants or token-based access.

arguments.name: allowed_oauth_flows_user_pool_client
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether the client is allowed to use OAuth 2.0 features. `allowed_oauth_flows_user_pool_client` must be set to `true` before you can configure the following arguments: `callback_urls`, `logout_urls`, `allowed_oauth_scopes` and `allowed_oauth_flows`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `allowed_oauth_flows_user_pool_client` argument enables OAuth 2.0 functionality for the Cognito user pool client, allowing users to configure advanced authentication flows such as callback URLs, logout URLs, OAuth scopes, and grant types. Setting this to `true` is essential for integrating the client with external applications that rely on OAuth-based authentication and authorization workflows.

arguments.name: allowed_oauth_scopes
arguments.description: (Optional) List of allowed OAuth scopes, including `phone`, `email`, `openid`, `profile`, and `aws.cognito.signin.user.admin`. `allowed_oauth_flows_user_pool_client` must be set to `true` before you can configure this option.
arguments.llm_summary: The `allowed_oauth_scopes` argument for the `aws_cognito_user_pool_client` resource allows users to define the specific OAuth scopes (e.g., `phone`, `email`, `openid`, `profile`, `aws.cognito.signin.user.admin`) that the client can request during authentication. Configuring this argument enables fine-grained control over the permissions granted to authenticated users, supporting secure and tailored access to user data and functionality within the Cognito user pool.

arguments.name: auth_session_validity
arguments.description: (Optional) Duration, in minutes, of the session token created by Amazon Cognito for each API request in an authentication flow. The session token must be responded to by the native user of the user pool before it expires. Valid values for `auth_session_validity` are between `3` and `15`, with a default value of `3`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `auth_session_validity` argument in the `aws_cognito_user_pool_client` resource allows users to define the duration (in minutes) of session tokens generated during authentication flows, ensuring tokens are valid for a specified time before requiring a response from the user. This configuration impacts session management by controlling token expiration, which is critical for balancing security and user experience in API interactions.

arguments.name: callback_urls
arguments.description: (Optional) List of allowed callback URLs for the identity providers. `allowed_oauth_flows_user_pool_client` must be set to `true` before you can configure this option.
arguments.llm_summary: The `callback_urls` argument in the `aws_cognito_user_pool_client` resource allows users to define a set of authorized callback URLs that identity providers can redirect to after successful authentication. This configuration is essential for enabling OAuth flows and ensuring secure redirection during user sign-in processes, particularly when `allowed_oauth_flows_user_pool_client` is set to `true`.

arguments.name: default_redirect_uri
arguments.description: (Optional) Default redirect URI and must be included in the list of callback URLs.
arguments.llm_summary: The `default_redirect_uri` argument for the `aws_cognito_user_pool_client` resource allows users to specify the primary URI to which authentication responses are redirected after successful user sign-in or sign-out. This URI must be included in the list of callback URLs, ensuring secure and consistent redirection behavior for OAuth 2.0 flows, typically used to configure the default endpoint for applications integrating with Cognito.

arguments.name: enable_propagate_additional_user_context_data
arguments.description: (Optional) Enables the propagation of additional user context data.
arguments.llm_summary: "Controls whether the `aws_cognito_user_pool_client` propagates additional user context data, such as device or application information, to downstream services during authentication flows. Enabling this argument enhances user context tracking, which can support advanced analytics, personalization, or security use cases."

arguments.name: enable_token_revocation
arguments.description: (Optional) Enables or disables token revocation.
arguments.llm_summary: The `enable_token_revocation` argument in the `aws_cognito_user_pool_client` resource allows users to control whether token revocation is enabled for the client, which impacts the ability to invalidate refresh tokens and prevent their reuse. Setting this argument to `true` enhances security by enabling token lifecycle management, aligning with common goals of securing authentication workflows and mitigating risks associated with compromised tokens.

arguments.name: explicit_auth_flows
arguments.description: (Optional) List of authentication flows. The available options include `ADMIN_NO_SRP_AUTH`, `CUSTOM_AUTH_FLOW_ONLY`, `USER_PASSWORD_AUTH`, `ALLOW_ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD_AUTH`, `ALLOW_CUSTOM_AUTH`, `ALLOW_USER_PASSWORD_AUTH`, `ALLOW_USER_SRP_AUTH`, `ALLOW_REFRESH_TOKEN_AUTH`, and `ALLOW_USER_AUTH`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `explicit_auth_flows` argument for the `aws_cognito_user_pool_client` resource allows users to specify the authentication methods and flows that the client supports, such as admin-based authentication, custom flows, or user password-based authentication. Configuring this argument enables fine-grained control over how users authenticate with the Cognito user pool, aligning the client’s behavior with specific security requirements or application use cases.

arguments.name: generate_secret
arguments.description: (Optional) Boolean flag indicating whether an application secret should be generated.
arguments.llm_summary: The `generate_secret` argument in the `aws_cognito_user_pool_client` resource allows users to specify whether an application secret should be automatically generated for the client. Enabling this feature enhances security by creating a unique secret key for client authentication, commonly used in scenarios requiring secure access to the Cognito user pool, such as OAuth flows or API integrations.

arguments.name: id_token_validity
arguments.description: (Optional) Time limit, between 5 minutes and 1 day, after which the ID token is no longer valid and cannot be used. By default, the unit is hours. The unit can be overridden by a value in `token_validity_units.id_token`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `id_token_validity` argument allows users to define the lifespan of ID tokens issued by the Cognito user pool client, specifying how long they remain valid before expiration. This configuration is essential for controlling token expiration policies, enhancing security, and aligning token validity with application requirements, with a default unit of hours that can be customized using `token_validity_units.id_token`.

arguments.name: logout_urls
arguments.description: (Optional) List of allowed logout URLs for the identity providers. `allowed_oauth_flows_user_pool_client` must be set to `true` before you can configure this option.
arguments.llm_summary: The `logout_urls` argument in the `aws_cognito_user_pool_client` resource allows users to define a set of URLs where users are redirected after logging out from the application. This configuration is essential for managing post-logout behavior in OAuth flows and ensures seamless user experience by directing users to appropriate endpoints. Note that `allowed_oauth_flows_user_pool_client` must be enabled to use this feature.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: (Required) Name of the application client.
arguments.llm_summary: The `name` argument for the `aws_cognito_user_pool_client` resource specifies the unique identifier for the application client within the associated Cognito User Pool. By defining this required string, users establish a recognizable and human-readable name for the client, which is essential for managing and referencing the application in authentication workflows, integrations, and API interactions.

arguments.name: prevent_user_existence_errors
arguments.description: (Optional) Setting determines the errors and responses returned by Cognito APIs when a user does not exist in the user pool during authentication, account confirmation, and password recovery.
arguments.llm_summary: The `prevent_user_existence_errors` argument in the `aws_cognito_user_pool_client` resource allows users to control how Cognito APIs handle authentication, account confirmation, and password recovery errors when a user does not exist in the user pool. By configuring this behavior, users can enhance security and privacy by preventing error messages that might reveal whether a user account exists, aligning with common goals like mitigating enumeration attacks.

arguments.name: read_attributes
arguments.description: (Optional) List of user pool attributes that the application client can read from.
arguments.llm_summary: The `read_attributes` argument in the `aws_cognito_user_pool_client` resource allows users to specify a set of user pool attributes that the application client is permitted to read. Configuring this argument enables fine-grained control over the data accessible to the client, supporting secure and tailored user data retrieval based on application requirements.

arguments.name: refresh_token_validity
arguments.description: (Optional) Time limit, between 60 minutes and 10 years, after which the refresh token is no longer valid and cannot be used. By default, the unit is days. The unit can be overridden by a value in `token_validity_units.refresh_token`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `refresh_token_validity` argument in the `aws_cognito_user_pool_client` resource allows users to define the duration, ranging from 60 minutes to 10 years, for which a refresh token remains valid before expiration. This configuration impacts token lifecycle management, enabling users to control how long clients can request new access tokens without requiring reauthentication, which is critical for balancing security and user experience in authentication workflows.

arguments.name: supported_identity_providers
arguments.description: (Optional) List of provider names for the identity providers that are supported on this client. It uses the `provider_name` attribute of the `aws_cognito_identity_provider` resource(s), or the equivalent string(s).
arguments.llm_summary: The `supported_identity_providers` argument for the `aws_cognito_user_pool_client` resource allows users to specify a set of identity providers (e.g., social login providers or external authentication systems) that the client can integrate with, using their `provider_name` attributes. Configuring this argument enables the user pool client to support authentication via these external providers, facilitating multi-provider login options and enhancing user authentication flexibility.

arguments.name: user_pool_id
arguments.description: (Required) User pool the client belongs to. The following arguments are optional:
arguments.llm_summary: The `user_pool_id` argument specifies the unique identifier of the Cognito User Pool to which the client application belongs, enabling the association of the client with a specific user authentication and management environment. By setting this required argument, users define the scope of the client’s operations, such as user sign-in, sign-up, and token generation, within the context of the designated User Pool.

arguments.name: write_attributes
arguments.description: (Optional) List of user pool attributes that the application client can write to.
arguments.llm_summary: The `write_attributes` argument in the `aws_cognito_user_pool_client` resource allows users to specify a set of user pool attributes that the application client is permitted to modify. Configuring this argument enables fine-grained control over which user profile fields can be updated by the client, supporting use cases like managing user data updates while enforcing attribute-level access restrictions.

blocks.name: analytics_configuration
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration block for Amazon Pinpoint analytics that collects metrics for this user pool. See details below.

arguments.name: application_arn
arguments.description: (Optional) Application ARN for an Amazon Pinpoint application. Conflicts with `external_id` and `role_arn`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `application_arn` argument in the `analytics_configuration` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool_client` resource allows users to specify the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of an Amazon Pinpoint application for analytics integration. By setting this argument, users can enable detailed tracking and analysis of user pool client activity through Pinpoint, facilitating advanced metrics and insights. Note that it conflicts with `external_id` and `role_arn`, ensuring a single method of analytics configuration is used.

arguments.name: application_id
arguments.description: (Optional) Application ID for an Amazon Pinpoint application.
arguments.llm_summary: The `application_id` argument in the `analytics_configuration` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool_client` resource specifies the Amazon Pinpoint application to associate with the user pool client for analytics tracking. By setting this argument, users can enable detailed user behavior analysis and engagement metrics, aligning the Cognito client with a specific Pinpoint application for targeted insights and reporting.

arguments.name: external_id
arguments.description: (Optional) ID for the Analytics Configuration. Conflicts with `application_arn`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `external_id` argument in the `analytics_configuration` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool_client` resource allows users to specify a unique identifier for the associated analytics configuration. This ID is typically used to link the user pool client to an external analytics service, enabling tracking and analysis of user behavior. It cannot be used simultaneously with `application_arn`, ensuring a clear and conflict-free configuration.

arguments.name: role_arn
arguments.description: (Optional) ARN of an IAM role that authorizes Amazon Cognito to publish events to Amazon Pinpoint analytics. Conflicts with `application_arn`.
arguments.llm_summary: Defines the ARN of an IAM role that grants Amazon Cognito permission to publish user pool analytics events to Amazon Pinpoint, enabling detailed event tracking and analysis. This argument is optional and conflicts with `application_arn`, allowing users to specify the authorization mechanism for analytics integration.

arguments.name: user_data_shared
arguments.description: (Optional) If set to `true`, Amazon Cognito will include user data in the events it publishes to Amazon Pinpoint analytics.
arguments.llm_summary: Controls whether Amazon Cognito includes user data in analytics events sent to Amazon Pinpoint, enabling detailed user behavior tracking for insights and engagement optimization. Setting this to `true` allows integration with Pinpoint for advanced analytics, supporting goals like user segmentation and campaign performance analysis.

blocks.llm_summary: The `analytics_configuration` block within the `aws_cognito_user_pool_client` resource enables integration with Amazon Pinpoint to collect and analyze user pool metrics, supporting advanced analytics and user behavior tracking. It encapsulates settings related to configuring Pinpoint analytics, such as specifying the application and role for data collection, allowing users to monitor and optimize user engagement and application performance.

blocks.name: token_validity_units
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration block for representing the validity times in units. See details below. Detailed below.

arguments.name: access_token
arguments.description: (Optional) Time unit in for the value in `access_token_validity`, defaults to `hours`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `access_token` argument within the `token_validity_units` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool_client` resource allows users to specify the time unit (e.g., hours, minutes, or days) for the validity duration of access tokens issued by the Cognito user pool. Configuring this argument helps define the expiration behavior of access tokens, aligning token lifetimes with application security requirements and session management goals.

arguments.name: id_token
arguments.description: (Optional) Time unit in for the value in `id_token_validity`, defaults to `hours`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `id_token` argument within the `token_validity_units` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool_client` resource allows users to specify the time unit (e.g., hours, days, etc.) for the validity duration of ID tokens issued by the Cognito user pool. Configuring this argument helps define the expiration behavior of ID tokens, aligning token lifetimes with application security and session management requirements.

arguments.name: refresh_token
arguments.description: (Optional) Time unit in for the value in `refresh_token_validity`, defaults to `days`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `refresh_token` argument within the `token_validity_units` block of the `aws_cognito_user_pool_client` resource specifies the time unit (e.g., days, hours, etc.) used to define the validity duration of refresh tokens via the `refresh_token_validity` setting. Configuring this argument allows users to control the expiration behavior of refresh tokens, which impacts session management and user authentication workflows in Cognito.

blocks.llm_summary: The `token_validity_units` configuration block within the `aws_cognito_user_pool_client` resource defines the time units (e.g., seconds, minutes, hours, or days) used to specify the validity durations for various tokens, such as access, refresh, and ID tokens. This block enables precise control over token expiration settings, helping users tailor authentication workflows to meet security and usability requirements.

attributes.name: client_secret
attributes.description: Client secret of the user pool client.

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: ID of the user pool client.
